newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: NSW's Carr says BHP Newcastle move tragic.
newsitem.headline: NSW's Carr says BHP Newcastle move tragic.

text.p: The premier of the Australian state of South Wales, Bob Carr, said he would travel to Newcastle later on Tuesday to assess first-hand the effect of the Broken Hill Pty Co's decision to shut down steelmaking facilities there.
Carr said the decision was tragic for the workers there and for the Australian economy. The Federal government's lack of any action to stop the shut-down was disappointing, he said.

"This is bad news for the Hunter and it's bad news for manufacturing in Australia," Carr told reporters after announcing the beginning of construction at Fox's new film and television studios in Sydney.
"To lose such a chunk of steel making capacity is tragic, not just for the workers, but for this country and its capacity to make things," Carr said.
"I think it's important that I be there to meet the workers and the union to understand first hand what they and their families are suffering," he said.
BHP announced earlier it would shut down the steel making facilities at Newcastle by 1999, but expand the existing bar, rod and wire mills.
The restructuring would cost 2,500 jobs, BHP said.

Carr said the forces at work in the global steel making industry had pushed BHP towards this latest move and that state and federal governments were unlikely to have been able to stop such a restructuring.
"This goes well beyond the capacity of the state government and even the federal government," he said.
"It's been done predominantly because of BHP's assessment of the global factors in steelmaking," he said.
